content.title: About
content.content: Snowpeas are frozen pea pods that have been pre‑cooked and contain no added fat. They retain the sweet flavor and crisp texture of fresh peas while being ready to heat and serve.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Snowpeas are often called “snow peas” because of their pale green color after freezing.
Heat processing locks in most B‑vitamins and vitamin C.
Freezing occurs immediately after harvest, preserving peak freshness.
Pea pods are a good source of plant protein and dietary fiber.
Snowpeas can be added directly to hot dishes without thawing.

items.title: Rich in plant protein
items.content: A serving provides about 5 g of protein, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: No added fat makes it suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Vitamins and minerals
items.content: Contains vitamin C, vitamin K, folate, iron, and magnesium, important for immunity and metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidant compounds
items.content: Phytonutrients in peas help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Legume allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to pea family members.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain batches may be lightly salted; check the label if you monitor sodium intake.

items.title: Freezing‑related quality issues
items.content: Improper storage can cause ice crystal formation and degrade texture.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Add Snowpeas to soups, stews, pasta, stir‑fries, or simply heat them as a side dish in the microwave or on a skillet. They also work well in salads after a quick sauté.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen Snowpeas in a freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. Once thawed, use within 2–3 days and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
